summary: Baileys fork performs on-import beacon fetch to author-controlled mutable GitHub URL
details: @alannxd/baileys is a third-party fork of the @whiskeysockets/baileys WhatsApp library. When the package is imported, lib/index.js unconditionally performs an HTTPS GET to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information.json and prints the first element of the response to the console. The fetched content is treated as a string for display only — it is not passed to eval/Function/exec, and no installer data is sent in the request body. However, every consumer's IP address is revealed to the author on each import, and the URL points to a mutable branch on a personal GitHub repository, so the content can be changed by the author at any time without a new package release. Additionally, the package name closely mirrors the well-known @whiskeysockets/baileys library and may be installed by mistake by users expecting the upstream. The lib/Utils/generics.js reference to 'ping' is a benign network-reachability helper, not exfiltration. As written, the package does not exfiltrate credentials, execute remote code, or destroy installer-side resources, so it falls below the block threshold; however, the import-time beacon to a mutable author-controlled source and the namespace-confusion risk warrant human review.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
